title: Node drain tolerance and cascade fallback playbook
content:
Context and intent:

This is an operational playbook drafted for private deployments (VPC and on-prem appliance) focused on:
- node-level drain tolerance during runtime/control-plane upgrades,
- preventing cascade failures when API compatibility shims are removed, and
- an explicit sequence to perform phased rollouts and automated rollback triggers.

This doc is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive: small commands, gating checks, telemetry thresholds, and terraform module notes intended for the SRE/ops engineer performing the cutover. Treat as a living document; expect additional checklist items after the first couple of cutovers.

High-level strategy summary:
1) Shadow traffic and canary circuits for the new runtime variant for 48–72 hours. Mirror 5–10% of real traffic and synthetic traffic against new build.
2) Gradual node replacement using drain-tolerant configuration: ensure KV cache warm-start and persistent shards can survive node removal without evicting active sessions.
3) API-level compatibility gate: deploy a lightweight compatibility shim sidecar on nodes where we are removing older endpoints. Compatibility shim provides a 1:1 translation for deprecated fields until telemetry confirms zero real usage.
4) Automated rollback triggers: latency > 2x baseline OR error-rate spike > 1% absolute for 5 minutes triggers automatic traffic reroute and scaled rollback.

Prereqs / assumptions:
- Terraform-managed clusters (k8s or appliance fleet) with a controlled upgrade pipeline.
- Runtime and control plane support for live KV import/export and reconnect semantics.
- Observability: per-route request latency, error rate, token-level cost metrics, and a synthetic traffic harness available per site.
- Clear canary and prod tagging in Console/Controlplane that the routing layer can use.

Terminology quick notes (how I use words in this doc):
- draining node: taking the node out of active routing while preserving ephemeral KV/shard state if possible.
- cascade failure: a multi-node outage triggered by a single node removal (often due to poor cache salvage).
- compat-shim: a sidecar or shim image that translates deprecated API shapes to the new shape to avoid client breakage.

Runbook: pre-upgrade checklist (operator tasks):
- Announce maintenance window to customer (if dedicated) and internal slack channel ops-private-upgrades.
- Snapshot control-plane DB and runtime KV store. Verify integrity hash.
- Confirm synthetic harness for the site is enabled and running baseline tests.
- Confirm terraform plan shows only intended changes; stash plan output in artifact store.
- Make sure autoscale limits are increased by +20% to handle temporary load spikes during drain.

Node replacement sequence (step-by-step):
1) Pick a single zone/row to start (avoid distributed blast radius).
2) Mark nodes in zone as candidate-canary in controlplane routing.
3) Deploy new runtime onto candidate nodes with compat-shim enabled by default.
4) Start traffic mirroring (5% user traffic + 100% synthetic). Monitor for 30–60 minutes.
   - Watch for: 500s, 502/503 patterns, tail latency P99, and token-cost deltas.
5) If stable, promote candidate nodes to canary: route 10–20% production traffic. Continue to monitor for 2–4 hours.
6) Begin draining a single old node from the zone: use graceful drain so long-lived sessions have a chance to failover (k8s: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300). For appliance: set node state=draining via admin API.
7) Verify KV reconciliation on replacement node (check runtime logs for warm-start success and shard reclaim).
8) If no regressions after 1 hour, repeat drain for additional nodes in zone in batches of 2.

Terraform module notes (working tactics / gotchas):
- Use lifecycle.ignore_changes for fields that are managed by the runtime agent at boot (e.g., dynamic ip lists) to avoid drift flip-flopping.
- Add a boolean flag `compat_shim_enabled` to the node template so we can toggle shim without changing image tags. This avoids a full instance replacement.
- When changing resource names for new runtime, prefer adding new resources and gradual cutover vs. in-place replacement to prevent terraform destroy/create cycles that cause multi-node churn.
- Keep a `pre_upgrade_snapshot` tag on instances managed by TF; the apply should fail if the snapshot tag is missing. This is enforced via a pre-apply validation script.

Compatibility shim design notes (short):
- shim listens on local port and exposes legacy endpoints. Routes translate into new request shape and inject a compatibility header X-Compat-Shim: true for telemetry.
- shim must be opt-out via runtime flag; default ON for the first 2 release windows.
- lightweight binary (static) to reduce image vulnerabilities; minimal deps.

Telemetry and SLO gating (conservative thresholds for automated rollback):
- Latency: P99 > baseline*1.8 for 10m => open rollback window.
- Error: increase of absolute 1% (e.g., from 0.2% to 1.2%) for 5m => immediate partial rollback to 50% traffic for canary nodes.
- Token-cost regressions: per-token CPU/gpu cost > 15% across canary => hold rollout and investigate.
- KV-miss rate: if KV miss rate on warm-start > 10% for first 30 minutes, abort further node drains and revert.

Rollback choreography (manual and automated):
- Automated: routing controller flips traffic away from canary nodes to stable pool. This is only triggered by configured alerts.
- Manual rollback steps:
  1) Put new nodes into maintenance mode (controlplane API -> set routing weight=0).
  2) Re-enable old images/instances via terraform (if they were cordoned) or restore snapshot.
  3) Rehydrate KV from snapshot if reconciliation failed.
  4) Mark the release as blocked in release tracker and open a postmortem ticket.

Post-cutover validation checklist (10–30 minutes after each batch):
- run synthetic end-to-end scenario A–C (latency, returned tokens, correctness heuristics).
- spot-check 3 randomly sampled long-running sessions to ensure no hallucinated state.
- confirm Console metrics: token-rate, per-route latency, and error-rate look normal.
- validate deploy trace IDs exist and are searchable for new nodes.

Operational anti-patterns observed (lessons learned):
- Draining too many nodes in same rack caused HDD/DB leader elections in appliance environment. Always space replacements across racks.
- Immediate removal of compat-shim caused a thin tail of requests that still used deprecated fields; these generated client-side 4xx noise. Keep shim for at least 2 release cycles after a major deprecation.
- Using terraform in-place rename for critical instance groups produced transient duplicate hostnames; prefer create-then-retire pattern.

Open questions / TODOs (action items):
- We should build a small canary harness that injects realistic token patterns including KV-warm sessions (followup: PR to runtime repo to add harness).
- Automate the snapshot verification step into the TF pipeline as a precondition gate (owner: Marta).
- Decide on a firm policy for compat-shim expiry: propose 2 release windows after deprecation announcement, then hard cut.

Appendix: quick control-plane commands and checks (notes to ops)
- Check canary routing weights: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://controlplane.site/api/v1/routing/canaries
- Set node draining state (appliance): POST /admin/nodes/:id/state {state: draining}
- Verify KV warm-start logs: grep "kv-warm-start" /var/log/runtime/agent.log | tail -n 200
- Terraform: terraform plan -var=compat_shim_enabled=true -out=plan.out; terraform apply plan.out

If anything here is unclear or you run into a situation not covered, ping #ops-private-upgrades and escalate to SRE lead (Ava) before proceeding with more than one node per zone.

Revision history:
- 2024-10-15: initial draft (Samir)
- 2024-11-02: added terraform lifecycle hints and compat-shim design (Marta)
- 2024-11-20: tightened telemetry thresholds and added automated rollback flow (Ava)

End of doc.
